blocks.title: MIA — check bags & security
blocks.detail:
• Aer Lingus check-in, Terminal E
• Bags tag straight through to Paris — this is the only check-in of the outbound
• Three hours before departure is right for a holiday-week transatlantic

blocks.title: Early dinner at MIA
blocks.detail:
Likely Terminal: Central
Options: Burger King, Chick Fil-A

blocks.title: Aer Lingus 140 · MIA → DUB (overnight) — BOOKED
blocks.detail:
Duration: 8h15 — 7:05 PM Miami → 8:20 AM Dublin (T2)
Aircraft: Airbus A330-300
Seats: 33H, 33K, 34H, 34K
Meals: hot dinner about 90 min after take-off, wine or beer included; juice before landing. Child meals free but must be booked BY PHONE 48h+ ahead
Luggage: 1 checked bag each, tagged through to Paris
blocks.program: Alaska Mileage Plan — Aer Lingus award

days.title: Arrive Paris — the tower lit, and dinner at its foot

blocks.title: Dublin connection — 1h35
blocks.detail:
• Both flights are Terminal 2; bags are checked through — no baggage hall, no customs
• Follow FLIGHT CONNECTIONS → Irish passport control (non-EU queue, or the e-gates if offered to US passports) → transfer security (hand-bag X-ray: empty water bottles, liquids under 100 ml) → gate
• Transatlantic flights use the T2 400-gates. EI 524 normally leaves from the 400-gates too; if the screens show a 100- or 200-gate that is Terminal 1, a 10–15 minute walk by the internal link
• Allow 45–60 minutes for the process, then buy lunch airside to eat on EI 524 — there is no meal on board and nothing to buy at CDG before immigration
blocks.flag: 1h35 is above Aer Lingus's published 90-minute minimum for a same-ticket connection; if EI 140 is late, Aer Lingus rebooks you on the next Paris flight. Go straight to passport control first.

blocks.title: Aer Lingus 524 · DUB → CDG
blocks.detail:
Duration: 1h50 — 9:55 AM Dublin → 12:45 PM Paris CDG Terminal 1
Aircraft: Airbus A320
Seats: 20A, 20B, 20C, 20D
Meals: none — eat what you bought airside in Dublin
Luggage: checked bags already through to Paris
blocks.notes: Same ticket as EI 140.

blocks.title: CDG Terminal 1 — passport control & bags
blocks.detail:
• Ireland is outside Schengen, so this is a full external-border arrival
• EU Entry/Exit System: passport scan, photo and fingerprints for the adults; children under 12 are photo and scan only
• Baggage claim and the arrivals hall are on Level 5
• Typical: 45–60 minutes from the gate to the arrivals hall
blocks.flag: T1 queues of 60–90 minutes have been reported at peak since EES started. If it runs long, everything after shifts; the evening still fits because dinner has no fixed sitting time.

blocks.title: Taxi rank — Level 5, Exit 24
blocks.detail:
• Official rank is on the arrivals level (Level 5), Exit 24, past the car-rental desks
• Use the marked rank only — ignore anyone offering a ride in the hall
• Ask for a van (monospace) so all four and the bags fit in one car

blocks.title: Taxi CDG → Hyatt Regency Paris Étoile
blocks.detail:
• Regulated flat rate: €56 to the Right Bank (Porte Maillot, 17th), up to 4 passengers, luggage included, no surcharges
• 30 km by the A1 and the périphérique, 40–45 minutes at this hour
• Card accepted; the fare is fixed, not metered
blocks.notes: €56 flat rate, tariff of 1 Feb 2026.

blocks.title: Check in — Hyatt Regency Paris Étoile, 4 nights, 2 rooms — BOOKED
blocks.detail:
• 3 Place du Général Kœnig, 75017 Paris
• Check-in from 15:00; early check-in requested on 31438883
• Ask for connecting or adjoining rooms
• Métro 1, RER C and RER E directly underneath
blocks.roomType: 2 × Twin room (2 twin beds), 1 adult + 1 child each
blocks.notes: Two reservations, 60,000 points each. Checkout 12:00. City tax €8.45 per person aged 13+ per night — €67.60 for the stay, paid at checkout.
blocks.flag: Confirm at check-in that breakfast covers both rooms.

blocks.title: Rooms — shower, unpack, rest
blocks.detail:
• 1h45. You have been travelling since 16:00 yesterday
• Shower and change for dinner — this is the night the dress shirt comes out

blocks.title: Bus 82 · Porte Maillot → Trocadéro
blocks.detail:
• One bus, no change, no stairs. 16 minutes on board, about 26 minutes door to door
• Stop is on Place du Trocadéro itself
• €2 per adult

blocks.title: Trocadéro — first sight of the tower, lit
blocks.detail:
• The terrace between the two wings of the Palais de Chaillot: the full-height view, and the best first sight of the tower in Paris
• Sunset 16:54, so it is fully lit before you arrive
• It sparkles for 5 minutes at 18:00 — that is what you are here for
• Free

blocks.title: Walk down to Port de Suffren
blocks.detail:
• Through the Trocadéro gardens, across Pont d'Iéna directly beneath the tower, then right along the river — 850 m, 12 minutes on Google, mostly flat
• 20 minutes budgeted: it is dark and the bridge is slow just after the sparkle

blocks.title: Dinner — Francette
blocks.detail:
• 1 Port de Suffren, 75007 — a barge moored opposite the tower, with a rooftop penthouse
• 4.5 from 9,226 Google reviews
• OPEN 12:00–01:00 EVERY DAY with no break in service, so 18:30 is a normal seating and there is no second-service turnover
• Mains €25–29: roast chicken with confit potatoes €26, beef tartare and chips €25, duck breast €29
• No children's menu, but the chicken and the pasta split easily
blocks.notes: About €115 for four with water: two mains and two desserts for the adults, two shared plates for the children.
blocks.flag: BOOKING OPENS ABOUT 17 NOVEMBER — SevenRooms runs a 30-day window. Book 18:30 for four, choose the indoor room not the terrace, then email reservation@francette.paris quoting the confirmation and ask for a table on the tower side. Restaurant +33 6 68 94 26 82. The linked carte is the SUMMER 2026 one.

blocks.title: RER C · Champ de Mars–Tour Eiffel → Neuilly–Porte Maillot
blocks.detail:
• 8 minutes on foot from the barge to the station, then 17 minutes on the train
• Trains every 15 minutes; the station is under the hotel
blocks.flag: Hotel by about 20:50 — a humane end to a 28-hour day.

days.title: Up the Eiffel Tower, then the Latin Quarter

blocks.title: Breakfast — hotel
blocks.detail: • Included

blocks.title: RER C · Neuilly–Porte Maillot → Champ de Mars–Tour Eiffel
blocks.detail:
• Station is under the hotel. 17 minutes on the train, about 30 minutes door to door including both walks
• Trains every 15 minutes
• €2.55 per adult, children 4–9 half price

blocks.title: Eiffel Tower — 2nd floor, then 1st floor
blocks.detail:
• Timed lift tickets for 10:00: €23.50 adult, €6 child aged 4–11 = €59 for four
• Arrive about 15 minutes before the slot. Earlier only means waiting outside, and more than 20 minutes late is not guaranteed entry
• Security check, lift to the 2nd floor for the views, then down to the 1st floor for the glass floor and the Christmas winter terrace
• Lift tickets go on sale 60 days ahead at midnight Paris time — 19 October. They sell out
blocks.flag: Not the summit: a second lift, a second queue, and wind at 276 m in December. The 2nd floor is the right height with a 5-year-old.

blocks.title: RER C · Champ de Mars–Tour Eiffel → Saint-Michel–Notre-Dame
blocks.detail:
• 4 stops, 9–11 minutes on the train. About 30 minutes door to door, 45 budgeted
• Getting down from the tower and out through the Champ de Mars crowds can take 15–20 minutes on its own — that is what the extra quarter hour is for
• Trains every 10–15 minutes off-peak
• €2.55 per adult, children 4–9 half price
blocks.flag: RER C is the single point of failure. If it is down, a taxi is 10–15 minutes and about €18.

blocks.title: Lunch — Latin Quarter, pick on the spot
blocks.detail:
Three that all sit on the cobbled medieval streets. Walk past, look in, choose.

1. LE PETIT CHÂTELET, 39 rue de la Bûcherie — about €84. The pick. Cobbled western end, two doors from Shakespeare and Company. UPSTAIRS ROOM WITH TWO DORMER WINDOWS FACING NOTRE-DAME, and a wood fire downstairs they grill on. TripAdvisor 4.4 from 2,066, #600 of 20,452. Chicken breast €19.50, duck confit €21, beef cheek €22.50, chocolate crêpes €7.50. Daily 12:00–14:15, closed only 25 Dec–1 Jan. PHONE ONLY +33 1 46 33 53 40 — ask for a table upstairs by a window.

2. LOUBNANE, 29 rue Galande — about €75. Best rated of the three, GOOGLE 4.6 FROM 2,677, and on rue Galande itself, the one street confirmed to be genuinely paved. Lebanese. Mains €20–25; the eight-dish mezze at €29 a head is built for sharing. Opens 12:00.

3. CHEZ HAMADI, 12 rue Boutebrie — about €52, the cheap one. A narrow medieval lane off rue de la Parcheminerie, one block behind Saint-Séverin and one street back from the tourist crush. Five minutes from the RER, the closest of the three. Tunisian; couscous €14.80, portions generous enough to share. TripAdvisor 4.0 from 297 — but some recent reviews report the kitchen slipping.

Also on the street: Bistro des Livres, 44 rue Galande, 4.7 from 1,733 — the best-rated address here, but its menu is a Canva slideshow with no readable prices, so it is unverified rather than rejected.
blocks.notes: Budgeted at the dearest of the three. Loubnane saves about $10, Chez Hamadi about $37.
blocks.flag: Only Le Petit Châtelet needs booking, and only by telephone, about three weeks ahead.

blocks.title: Walk up through the quarter to the Luxembourg
blocks.detail:
• 1.0 km, 16 minutes on Google; 30 budgeted because you are stopping
• Up rue Saint-Jacques, right into rue des Écoles past the SORBONNE and place de la Sorbonne, back to rue Saint-Jacques and the PANTHÉON, then straight down rue Soufflot to the garden gates
• Rue Soufflot is the grandest sightline in the quarter: Panthéon behind you, Luxembourg gates ahead

blocks.title: Jardin du Luxembourg
blocks.detail:
• In by the rue de Médicis gate at the foot of rue Soufflot
• PLAYGROUND: €3 a child, €1 an adult — €8 for the four of you. Two fenced zones, under-7s and 7–12s, so Chloe and Roque Luis may be split
• The CAROUSEL dates from 1879 and was designed by Charles Garnier, who built the Opéra. It still has the jeu de bagues — you grab brass rings off a wooden arm with a stick as you go round. About €2–4
• Free and always there: the grand basin and its ducks, the Medici Fountain, and the small-scale Statue of Liberty, which is a good thing to send the children hunting for
blocks.flag: HARD STOPS: the playground shuts about 15:50 and the garden itself at 16:30. NO SAILBOATS — they are out of the water until spring, so do not promise them. The puppet theatre is dark on term-time Fridays and the school holidays start the next day, so you miss it by one day.

blocks.title: Walk back down through the quarter
blocks.detail:
• 1.1 km, 16 minutes on Google; 30 budgeted
• Down boulevard Saint-Michel, then cut into the cobbles: rue Galande with its 14th-century carving of Saint Julien above no. 42, rue Saint-Julien-le-Pauvre, and rue de la Bûcherie past Shakespeare and Company
• Sunset is 16:54, so these streets are lit and emptying as you go through — which is when they look best
• Skip rue de la Huchette, the tourist strip

blocks.title: Notre-Dame from the outside, and the Christmas market
blocks.detail:
• The market is in SQUARE RENÉ-VIVIANI on quai de Montebello, 26 Nov – 27 Dec 2026 — about 40 artisan chalets, roast chestnuts, vin chaud, Santa in attendance, and free children's drawing workshops. The oldest tree in Paris is in the same square, a 1601 robinia propped on a concrete crutch
• Cross Pont au Double to the parvis for the façade. Free, no ticket, nothing to book
• You arrive just before sunset at 16:54 and leave in the dark — the best light of the day on the west front
blocks.flag: Going INSIDE is free but cannot be pre-booked: slots open 72 hours out, and the winter walk-up wait is 15–25 minutes. If the queue is short and everyone is still game, you have the slack. Skip the towers — 424 steps and barred to under-6s.

blocks.title: RER C · Saint-Michel–Notre-Dame → Neuilly–Porte Maillot
blocks.detail:
• One train, no change, and the station is under the hotel — the easiest return of any option in Paris
• About 20 minutes on the train, 30 door to door

blocks.title: Rest at the hotel
blocks.detail: • About an hour. Shorter than the 90 minutes on the 17th — the Latin Quarter costs you that

blocks.title: EVENING — to be decided
blocks.detail:
• Options on the table: the Nuits Indiennes lantern festival at the Jardin d'Acclimatation (€60, opens 18:00, 12 minutes away), or the La Défense Christmas market (free, Fridays to 23:00, one RER E stop)
• Dinner: Le Congrès Maillot, 3 minutes from the hotel, continuous service, kids' menu €10 and free under 6

days.title: Montmartre in the morning, Vaux-le-Vicomte's Christmas by night

blocks.title: Breakfast — hotel
blocks.detail:
• Included
• Coats, gloves and hats come with you — you are out until almost 22:00

blocks.title: Taxi · Hotel → Sacré-Cœur
blocks.detail:
• Taxi rank at Porte Maillot, outside the hotel
• 4.9 km — Google, set to depart Saturday 19 Dec 08:15: typically 14–26 minutes
• Drops you at the top of the hill, behind the basilica, so the kids skip the climb
• Meter: €3 pick-up + €1.66/km (Saturday-morning Tarif B) + slow-traffic time — about €13–18; +€4 if booked through the G7 app

blocks.title: Sacré-Cœur and the view over Paris
blocks.detail:
• Basilica open from 06:30, free
• At this hour the steps and the terrace are nearly empty — the best time of day for photos
• Sunrise is 08:42, so the city is in soft early light

blocks.title: Old Montmartre backstreets
blocks.detail:
• Rue du Chevalier de la Barre → Rue Cortot → Rue des Saules and the Clos Montmartre vineyard → Rue de l'Abreuvoir → La Maison Rose (the pink house)
• Cobbled, quiet, village-like — all free

blocks.title: Place du Tertre — the painters' square
blocks.detail:
• The artists set up from about 10:00, so the square is waking up as you arrive
• Portrait and silhouette artists work on the spot — agree the price before they start
• Free to wander

blocks.title: Down the hill to lunch
blocks.detail:
• Rue Norvins → Rue Lepic past the Moulin de la Galette windmill → Place des Abbesses and the Mur des Je t'aime → Boulevard de Clichy past the Moulin Rouge → Rue de Douai
• All downhill, about 1.8 km with photo stops

blocks.title: Lunch — Pink Mamma
blocks.detail:
• 20bis rue de Douai, 75009 — four-storey Italian trattoria under a glass roof, 4.7 from 52,619 Google reviews
• Saturday lunch 12:00–16:00
• Pizzas €13.50–21, pasta €15–35, tiramisù €8.50. No children's menu — a margherita each (€13.50) works for the kids
• Tap water is free
blocks.notes: About €86 for four on tap water: two margheritas for the kids (€27), truffle mafaldine (€22) and a Pistacchio Disco pizza (€19.50) for the adults, two tiramisù (€17).
blocks.flag: BOOKING OPENS 19 NOVEMBER AT 09:00 PARIS TIME (03:00 Miami) — 30-day window, website only. Book 12:00 for four. Some tables are kept for walk-ins if it's full.

blocks.title: Métro · Place de Clichy → Gare de Lyon
blocks.detail:
• 5-minute walk to Place de Clichy
• Line 13 to Saint-Lazare, change to line 14 to Gare de Lyon — Google, set to depart Saturday 19 Dec 13:15: 28 minutes; line 2 + line 1 from Pigalle takes 32
• Then about 8 minutes up to the main hall for line R
• €2.55 per adult, €1.30 per child (4–9)
blocks.flag: Not a taxi for this leg: Google gives 22–55 minutes by car on the Saturday before Christmas.

blocks.title: Train · Line R Gare de Lyon → Melun
blocks.detail:
• 14:16 from Gare de Lyon, arrive Melun 14:44 — 28 minutes, no change
• Line R runs at :16 and :46 past the hour; the 14:46 is the fallback
• Same €2.55 / €1.30 ticket as the métro — Melun is inside the Île-de-France flat fare
blocks.flag: Google warns it does not have the latest timetables for December — re-check on SNCF Connect the week before.

blocks.title: Châteaubus shuttle · Melun station → Vaux-le-Vicomte
blocks.detail:
• Pick-up on Avenue Gallieni, in front of the Café de la Gare, outside Melun station
• Runs every day during the school holidays, which start 19 December
• €12 return per adult, €7 per child — €38 for four; booking required
• Backup: taxi from the station rank, €20–25 each way (+€5 after dark)
blocks.flag: The 2026 shuttle timetable is not published yet ("bookings coming soon"). Book it with the entry tickets and match the outbound to the 14:44 arrival and the return to the 19:07 train.

blocks.title: Le Grand Noël — inside the château
blocks.detail:
• This year's theme: a journey around the world — each salon is a different country, with automata, lights and an immersive projection
• Timed entry slot — book 15:15. Self-guided, about 1 hour
• Open 10:30–21:00 on 19 December (last entry 19:00)
• Saturday / school-holiday prices: adults from €27.90, children 3–17 from €22.90 — at least €101.60 for four
blocks.flag: Tickets not on sale yet ("réservation à venir"). Online booking is compulsory and it often sells out — book as soon as it opens. Prices are "from", so Saturday may cost slightly more.

blocks.title: The garden at dusk — treasure hunt, ice rink, marshmallows
blocks.detail:
• Treasure hunt: each child gets a "little traveller's passport" and collects stamps around the garden — free, ages 3+, until 18:30, with a small prize at the end
• Ice rink in front of the château: €5 per person, pay on the spot, kids' skating aids provided — bring gloves
• Marshmallows toasted by the fire — free, until 18:30
• Sunset 16:55 — the garden lights come on around you
blocks.notes: Ice rink budgeted for all four (€20). Hot chocolate or crêpes at the Le Gourmet chalet by the rink — prices are not published, so allow about €20 extra in cash.

blocks.title: Light show on the château façade
blocks.detail:
• "Vaux-le-Vicomte, escale au pays des rêves" — projected across the 1,000 m² façade, about 8 minutes
• Shows at 18:00, 18:30 and 19:00 — take the 18:00
• Then a last lap of the lit garden and back to the gate

blocks.title: Châteaubus shuttle · Vaux-le-Vicomte → Melun station
blocks.detail:
• Included in the return shuttle ticket
• Taxi backup: ask the welcome desk to call one, €25–30 at night

blocks.title: RER D · Melun → Gare de Lyon
blocks.detail:
• 19:07 from Melun, arrive Gare de Lyon 20:04 — 57 minutes, no change
• Slower than line R, but there is no line R between 18:30 and 20:12 on a Saturday
• €2.55 per adult, €1.30 per child
blocks.flag: Alternative: stay for the 19:00 show and take the line R 20:12 (arrive 20:44) — 35 more minutes at Vaux, hotel about 22:30.

blocks.title: Walk to dinner
blocks.detail: • Out of the station onto Boulevard Diderot — L'Européen is directly opposite, 3 minutes

blocks.title: Dinner — L'Européen
blocks.detail:
• 21bis boulevard Diderot, 75012 — classic Belle Époque brasserie facing Gare de Lyon, 4.1 from 6,004 Google reviews
• Open every day 07:30 to midnight (01:00 Fri–Sat), no reservation needed at this hour
• "Express" set menu €27 (starter + main, or main + dessert): steak-frites, sea bream, ravioles, chocolate mousse
• Children's menu (under 12) €10: frankfurters, chicken or sea bream with chips, 2-scoop ice cream and a drink — FREE UNDER 6
blocks.notes: About €64 for four on tap water: two Express menus (€54), one children's menu (€10), Chloe's is free.
blocks.flag: The menu is only published in French.

blocks.title: Métro 1 · Gare de Lyon → Porte Maillot
blocks.detail:
• One line, no change — the station is under the hotel
• €2.55 per adult, €1.30 per child
blocks.flag: Hotel by about 22:00 — only 16:00 in Miami, so the kids' body clocks are fine.

days.title: Jardin d'Acclimatation in the morning, Montmartre at sunset

blocks.title: Breakfast — hotel
blocks.detail: • Included

blocks.title: Walk to the Jardin d'Acclimatation
blocks.detail:
• 15 minutes after breakfast for coats and bathrooms, then out the door at 09:30
• 1.4 km, flat, along avenue Charles de Gaulle and into the Bois de Boulogne — Google: 20 minutes
• 25 minutes budgeted with the kids, arriving 5 minutes before the gates open

blocks.title: Jardin d'Acclimatation — rides while the lines are short
blocks.detail:
• Paris's own amusement park, 4.3 from 20,619 Google reviews
• Sunday + school holidays: open 10:00–18:00, rides stop 17:30
• Go straight to the rides — the queues build from late morning on a holiday Sunday
• Height limits: Speed Rockets and Défi du Dragon need 120 cm alone, 100–120 cm with an adult; Rafting needs 110 cm. Measure the kids before you go
• Tribu Pass — admission and unlimited rides for four: about €121 online vs €163 at the gate on weekends and holidays. The park recommends the unlimited pass for children 80–130 cm because an adult must ride with them
blocks.flag: Buy the dated Tribu Pass online for 20 December — the web price moves with demand. Gate prices shown in the price list are the April–September 2026 ones. The Petit Train was closed for maintenance in September; check it is back.

blocks.title: Lunch — Le Relais de la Ferme
blocks.detail:
• Inside the park, in the old half-timbered farmhouse at the Ferme Saint-Hilaire, next to the Ouessant sheep
• Counter service, no reservation; weekends 11:00–17:30
• Adults: pizza (margherita, smoked salmon, bacon & mushroom, or burrata) or the stracciatella focaccia, plus a dessert — €12.90
• Kids (under 12): pizzetta margherita, crisps, a drink (Vittel or Oasis) and a dessert (applesauce, drinking yogurt or an ice lolly) — €10.90
blocks.notes: About €48 for four: two pizza-and-dessert deals (€25.80) and two kids' pizzetta menus (€21.80). Also on the menu: salmon penne €12.90 (or €15.90 with a dessert), pesto-and-burrata pasta salad €13.90, egg-mayo sandwich €7.20, crêpes from €3.90, brownie €3.60, tiramisu pot €4.60. A drink with an adult deal is +€2.90.
blocks.flag: The menu is only published in French. Alternative with table service: La Terrasse du Jardin — mains €22.90–24.60, kids' menu €19, about €84 for four.

blocks.title: The farm, the Ferris wheel and last rides
blocks.detail:
• The Ferme Saint-Hilaire is right outside the Relais — goats, sheep, the farmyard
• La Grande Roue (the Ferris wheel) for the view over the Bois de Boulogne
• One last ride each, then head for the Sablons exit at 14:05

blocks.title: Taxi · Jardin d'Acclimatation → Place du Tertre
blocks.detail:
• 15 minutes to walk out to the Sablons gate and meet the taxi — book it on the G7 app from inside the park at about 14:10
• 7.4 km — Google, set to depart Sunday 20 Dec 14:25: typically 16–30 minutes
• Drops you on rue Norvins at the edge of Place du Tertre — cars cannot enter the square
• Meter: €3 + €1.66/km (Sunday Tarif B) + slow-traffic time — about €18–25, plus €4 for the app booking

blocks.title: Place du Tertre — the painters' square
blocks.detail:
• In full swing on a Sunday afternoon: easels, portrait and silhouette artists
• Agree any portrait price before the artist starts
• Free to wander
blocks.flag: Holiday Sunday afternoon — this is Montmartre at its busiest. Phones zipped away, bags in front; pickpockets work the square and the basilica steps.

blocks.title: Old Montmartre backstreets
blocks.detail:
• Rue Norvins → Rue des Saules and the Clos Montmartre vineyard → Rue de l'Abreuvoir → La Maison Rose (the pink house) → Rue Cortot
• Cobbled, quieter than the square, all free

blocks.title: Sacré-Cœur at sunset
blocks.detail:
• Sunset about 16:55 — watch the city go from daylight to lights from the terrace in front of the basilica
• Basilica open until 22:30, free; the dome is extra and not worth it with the kids at dusk

blocks.title: Down the hill to dinner
blocks.detail:
• Steps down to Rue Tardieu → Place des Abbesses and the Mur des Je t'aime → Rue Lepic → Boulevard de Clichy past the lit Moulin Rouge → Rue de Douai
• About 1.2 km, all downhill — Google has Place du Tertre to Pink Mamma at 13 minutes; 35 budgeted for photos and small legs
• 5 minutes in hand before the doors open at 18:00

blocks.title: Dinner — Pink Mamma
blocks.detail:
• 20bis rue de Douai, 75009 — four-storey Italian trattoria under a glass roof, 4.7 from 52,619 Google reviews
• Sunday dinner from 18:00 — first seating, before it fills up
• Pizzas €13.50–21, pasta €15–35, tiramisù €8.50. No children's menu — a margherita each (€13.50) works for the kids
• Tap water is free
blocks.notes: About €86 for four on tap water: two margheritas for the kids (€27), truffle mafaldine (€22) and a Pistacchio Disco pizza (€19.50) for the adults, two tiramisù (€17).
blocks.flag: BOOKING OPENS 20 NOVEMBER AT 09:00 PARIS TIME (03:00 Miami) — 30-day window, website only. Book 18:00 for four. Some tables are kept for walk-ins.

blocks.title: Taxi · Pink Mamma → hotel
blocks.detail:
• 10 minutes after dinner to pay and get coats on; book the taxi on the G7 app at the table
• 4.6 km — Google, set to depart Sunday 20 Dec 19:20: typically 14–30 minutes
• Meter about €13–18, plus €4 for the app booking
• Métro alternative: line 2 from Blanche + RER C, 41 minutes including a 7-minute walk between stations — not worth it with tired kids

blocks.title: Repack for the mountains
blocks.detail:
• Winter gear and snow clothes to the top of the bags
• Tomorrow is a direct TGV to Annecy from Gare de Lyon at 09:46

blocks.title: Breakfast — Regency Club
blocks.detail:
• Included
• Lunch is not until about 14:00 in Annecy

blocks.title: Checkout
blocks.detail: • Confirm the taxi at the door

blocks.title: Taxi · hotel → Gare de Lyon
blocks.detail:
• 8.8 km via the Champs-Élysées. Google, set to Monday 21 December departing 08:15, gives typically 22–55 minutes — this block allows the worst case
• Métro 1 goes there direct in ~25 minutes, but with four people and winter luggage in Monday rush hour the taxi is the right call
• About €25–30, metered

blocks.title: Gare de Lyon — snacks for the train
blocks.detail:
• TGV INOUI to Annecy: check the departure board for the hall — Halls 1 and 2 are side by side
• Monop'Daily (Hall 2, level 0) or Paul for pastries, fruit and water
• Platform posts about 20 minutes before departure

blocks.title: TGV INOUI · Paris Gare de Lyon → Annecy
blocks.detail:
• DIRECT, 3h43, no changes — published timetable for Monday 21 December (also 06:45→10:38 and 12:46→16:34)
• Domestic TGV, so the Carte Avantage price cap applies: adults never pay more than €89
• Reserved seats — book four together
• Annecy station exit → the hotel is a five-minute walk
blocks.notes: Budgeted at $215 for four with the Carte Avantage. Floor about $150 at opening-day advance fares; ceiling about $270 at the cap. Sales for these dates open on 30 September — book that morning.
blocks.flag: Sales open 30 September — book that morning, on an exchangeable fare.

blocks.title: Off the train — walk to lunch
blocks.detail:
• Les Burgers de Papa is three minutes from the station exit, on the way into town
• Bags come with you — it is counter service, not a sit-down restaurant

blocks.title: Lunch — Les Burgers de Papa
blocks.detail:
• 11 rue Président Favre — three minutes from the station
• Counter service, no booking, served continuously — which matters, because this is past the point where most Annecy kitchens stop serving lunch
• Burger menus from €9.90; burger + fries + four breaded bites €14.50; there is a children's menu
blocks.notes: About €40 for four on tap water: two €14.50 combos and two children's menus.

blocks.title: Walk to the apartment
blocks.detail:
• About fifteen minutes with the bags, flat the whole way
• 18 rue Sainte-Claire is under the arcades, in through a courtyard entrance

blocks.title: Check in — 18 rue Sainte-Claire — BOOKED
blocks.detail:
• 18 Rue Sainte-Claire, 74000 Annecy — in the old town, on the arcaded street, in a quiet interior courtyard
• EARLY CHECK-IN AGREED: Julien confirmed by message on 16 September that his cleaner finishes by 13:00 on a normal day, has this date in her calendar and has said yes — he calls 14:00 guaranteed and the risk of change very low. Worst case you leave the bags while she finishes
• SELF CHECK-IN BY KEYPAD, and the posted time is 'after 16:00' with no closing time — so arriving later is never a problem either
• CHECKOUT 11:00 — earlier than a hotel, which shapes the last morning
• One bedroom with a queen, living room with a 160 cm sofa bed for Chloe and Roque Luis; bathroom with a SEPARATE WC
• Full kitchen (oven, microwave, dishwasher, Nespresso), balcony, linen and towels provided
• Washing machine, drying rack, central heating AND a portable heater — this is where the snow gear dries
• Walking: old town 0 min, castle 3, lake 4, train station 7
• Quiet hours 21:00–08:00. Maximum 4 guests
blocks.nights: 6 nights (Mon Dec 21 – Sun Dec 27) · Entire apartment
blocks.roomType: Entire one-bedroom apartment — queen + 160 cm sofa bed
blocks.notes: $1,273.81 all in, charged to Visa 6730 on 13 November 2026. Host Julien, +41 79 960 38 00; co-hosts Piccolo and Marina. Free cancellation until 16:00 on 21 November; partial refund until 16:00 on 14 December. Rated 4.97 over 143 reviews, Superhost, and Airbnb's 'perfect ratings from families' badge.
blocks.flag: NO CARBON MONOXIDE ALARM — Airbnb flags this and suggests bringing a portable detector. Six nights, two kids: worth the €20.

blocks.title: Le Pâquier and the lakefront — the last of the daylight
blocks.detail:
• Out through the Jardins de l'Europe and over the Pont des Amours to the big lakeside meadow: swans, ducks, the mountains behind
• Hands free, everything already dropped at the flat
• Dark by about 16:50, so this is the daylight the early check-in bought you
• Free, ten minutes from the door

blocks.title: Back through the old town — the Thiou and the Palais de l'Isle
blocks.detail:
• Under your own arcades on rue Sainte-Claire, down to the canal and the Palais de l'Isle from the bridge — lit by now
• All within five minutes of the door

blocks.title: Noël des Alpes — the market after dark
blocks.detail:
• 135+ artisan chalets from Quai de Vicenza through Place Saint-Maurice to the Jardins de l'Europe, plus Santa at Place de l'Ancienne Grenette
• FREE entry. Illuminations on the old town and the chalets along the canal
• Natural outdoor ICE RINK (about 450 m²) in the Jardins de l'Europe — you skate here on the 23rd
• 2025–26 edition ran 29 Nov – 4 Jan, 11:00–21:00 (21:30 Fri/Sat and holidays)
blocks.flag: 2026–27 dates are not yet published — the city posts them in October/November. Every recent edition has covered your dates.

blocks.title: Monoprix — first shop for the apartment
blocks.detail:
• 65 rue Carnot, five minutes from the door. Mon–Sat 08:30–20:45, CLOSED SUNDAY
• Breakfast things, water, fruit, snacks — you have a kitchen now, so this shop does more work than a hotel mini-bar run
• There is also a small supermarket and a bakery on your own street
• Carrefour City, 14 avenue de Chambéry by the station, is the Sunday option: 09:00–12:50

blocks.title: Dinner — Le Ramoneur Savoyard
blocks.detail:
• 7 rue Grenette, old town — six minutes on foot
• Savoyard since 1923. Closed Wednesdays out of season, so Monday is fine
• Weekday formules: entrée + plat or plat + dessert €21, menu du jour €25; full menus €31.50–33.50
• MENU ENFANT 'P'tits Malins' €12.90 — steak haché and fries, ham and fries, or babyflette, plus ice cream
• Reserve: 04 50 51 29 03
blocks.notes: About €68 for four on tap water: two €21 formules and two children's menus. Replaces Brasserie des Européens, whose cheapest adult main is €25 — €75 for the same four people. The Brasserie is the fallback if this is full: Esplanade de l'Hôtel de Ville, open every day, 04 50 45 00 81.

days.title: Le Semnoz — sledging above the lake, 25 minutes by taxi

blocks.title: Breakfast — Pain et Copains
blocks.detail:
• 42 rue Vaugelas, five minutes — opens 06:30 Tue–Sat
• Croissants, pains au chocolat, coffee; sit in or take back to the rooms
• Buy the packed lunch for the mountain here too if you would rather not eat at the top

blocks.title: Taxi · Annecy → Semnoz, Annecy-side car park
blocks.detail:
• RUE SAINTE-CLAIRE IS PEDESTRIAN — a taxi cannot reach the door. Agree a pickup point when you book: the station forecourt is easiest, since breakfast is at Pain et Copains two minutes away; Pont Perrière is the option if you skip the bakery and come straight from the flat
• About 25 minutes up the mountain road — book the night before: Taxi74 06 64 12 58 66
• Ask for the car park at the foot of the pistes on the ANNECY side (versant Annecy) — that is where Le Châtillon and the sledging are. The other car park, versant Bauges, is over the ridge
• Ask for a return pick-up at 15:00 from the same spot, or take the driver's number
• Metered, prefecture-regulated: roughly €35–55 each way
• Bus alternative: line S2 from Annecy Gare, €2 a head, 60 minutes
blocks.notes: Budgeted at €100 for the round trip. If the S2 bus appeals for one direction, the 15:45 down gets you home by 16:45 and saves about €45.

blocks.title: Semnoz — the sledging slopes
blocks.detail:
• 1,450–1,700 m, open ground above the tree line
• FREE toboggan piste, open every day 09:00–17:00. There is no lift — you walk back up the left-hand side of the piste each time
• Sledge hire at the chalet nordique de la Forêt: €5 for a half-day (09:00–13:00 or 12:00–17:00), €8 all day. No booking, and none is possible
• Also free at the top of the station: two marked zones for parets and yooners
blocks.notes: Three sledges at €8 for the day, about €24. Snow tubing is NOT available here in winter — the Semnoz runs it beside the summer toboggan track only; the tubing on this trip is at Le Grand-Bornand on the 24th.
blocks.flag: SNOW RECORD: Semnoz was shut over Christmas in 2018 (from 24 Dec) and 2022 (from 22 Dec, sledging area included); it opened on time in 2023 and just in time (21 Dec) in 2024. Check semnoz.fr's live status the night before. IF IT IS SHUT: swap this day with Thursday — Le Grand-Bornand's upper area has snowmaking and opened 7–16 December in every one of those years.

blocks.title: Lunch — Le Châtillon
blocks.detail:
• At the foot of the pistes on the Annecy side, by the car park the taxi drops you at — the station lists it as 'au pied des pistes versant Annecy'
• Open every midday from December to March. Parking and step-free access
• Croque with salad and fries €15.50, omelette and salad €14.50–17, tartiflette €22, burger €21, fondue savoyarde €21 a head
• MENU ENFANT (under 10) €12 — ham and fries, nuggets and fries or mini tartiflette, plus compote or a madeleine
• 04 50 05 45 83
blocks.notes: About €55 for four on tap water: two croques and two children's menus. Replaces Le 1407, which the station lists as a winter-only snack bar on the Bauges-side car park — the wrong side of the ridge, and it publishes no menu.

blocks.title: Second run — snow play until the taxi
blocks.detail:
• Back on the sledges, or snowmen and snowball fights on the open ground
• Stop at 14:50; the taxi is at 15:00

blocks.title: Taxi · Semnoz → Annecy old town
blocks.detail: • 25 minutes, back to the same pedestrian-edge pickup point

blocks.title: Back at the apartment — dry everything out
blocks.detail:
• Gloves, hats, socks and base layers onto the drying rack by a radiator — the flat has central heating and a portable heater
• Boots opened out with newspaper inside; a tumble dryer would not touch them anyway
• Snow trousers and jackets air-dry only, never on direct heat — it ruins the waterproofing
• The washing machine is here if a load is worth doing tonight; Thursday is the other snow day

blocks.title: Market at dusk — Santa & crêpes
blocks.detail:
• Santa's chalet at Place de l'Ancienne Grenette; crêpes under the arcades
• Lights on from about 16:50

blocks.title: Dinner — Le Fréti
blocks.detail:
• 12 rue Sainte-Claire — SIX DOORS DOWN from the apartment at number 18
• Open seven days, all year: 12:00–14:00 and 18:30–22:30
• Fondues are priced PER PERSON: house La Fréti €19.90, traditional savoyarde €23, mushroom €24–27
• LA BRISGOTTE, under 10s, €12.50 — mini tartiflette or mini croziflette served in a hollowed loaf, plus two scoops of ice cream or a crêpe
• Reserve: 04 50 51 29 52 — it fills every winter evening
blocks.notes: About €65 for four on tap water: two La Fréti fondues at €19.90 and two Brisgottes.
blocks.flag: Book the 22nd and the 26th on the same call.

days.title: Annecy — château, lake & the market rink

blocks.title: Breakfast — Pain et Copains
blocks.detail: • Everything today is within ten minutes on foot

blocks.title: Walk up to the château
blocks.detail: • About fifteen minutes from the bakery, the last stretch up to the gate steep — it opens at 10:00

blocks.title: Château d'Annecy
blocks.detail:
• Winter hours 10:00–12:30 and 14:00–17:30. CLOSED TUESDAYS and 24–25 December — which is why it is today
• €6.50 adult, UNDER-12s FREE — €13 for the family
• Lake archaeology, medieval rooms, the ramparts — 90 minutes covers it
• The tourist office runs a family trail, 'Le château à petits pas' — ask at the desk

blocks.title: Lunch — La Bolée crêperie
blocks.detail:
• 41 rue Carnot, old town, since 1979 — four minutes down from the château
• Open Tue–Sat 11:45–22:30. Closed Sunday and Monday
• Savoury galettes €12.50–14.50 (savoyarde and brestoise €13, warm goat cheese €12.50)
• CHILDREN'S GALETTES €6.20–9.60 — butter, ham, cheese, egg and sausage combinations
• Sweet crêpes from €5.20; flambéed €7.50–10.50
blocks.notes: About €55 for four on tap water: two galettes at €13, two children's galettes, and two sweet crêpes to share.

blocks.title: Le Pâquier & the lakefront
blocks.detail:
• Across the Pont des Amours to the big lakeside meadow — swans, ducks, room to run
• Flat, free

blocks.title: Ice skating — the market rink, Jardins de l'Europe
blocks.detail:
• The Noël des Alpes outdoor rink, about 450 m², in the gardens — ten minutes round the lake end from the Pâquier
• Skate hire on site
blocks.notes: Price not published — market rinks of this size run €5–8 with skates. Budgeted at €25 for four.
blocks.flag: Indoor alternative: Patinoire Jean Régis, 90 chemin des Fins, 04 50 57 56 02 — you go there on Saturday anyway.

blocks.title: Goûter — crêpes
blocks.detail: • A market chalet or any café on Place Saint-Maurice

blocks.title: Noël des Alpes — chalets and Santa
blocks.detail:
• Santa's chalet at Place de l'Ancienne Grenette; artisan chalets along Quai de Vicenza and rue du Collège-Chappuisien
• Tomorrow the chalets close early (about 19:00)

blocks.title: Dinner — Le Napoli
blocks.detail:
• 8 rue du Pâquier — four minutes from the hotel
• Its own site gives 11:45–14:30 and 18:45–22:30 daily, evenings only on Saturday. Wednesday works
• Pizza margherita €12, napolitaine €14.50, buffala €17; tagliatelle carbonara €15.50, beef lasagne €17.50
• Reserve: 04 50 51 76 06
blocks.notes: About €54 for four on tap water: two adult dishes and two margheritas. No children's menu is published — ask when you book.
blocks.flag: Google lists this as closed Mondays, the restaurant's own site says open. Confirm on the phone; it changes nothing for a Wednesday.

days.title: Le Grand-Bornand — village sledging & tubing, then Christmas Eve

blocks.title: Breakfast — Pain et Copains, and the mountain snacks
blocks.detail:
• Opens 06:30
• Buy a sandwich each and snacks for the slopes
• Snow gear on; spare gloves and socks in the bag

blocks.title: Walk to the gare routière
blocks.detail:
• You are already by the station after breakfast — the coach station is 50 m to the right as you leave the railway station, three minutes from Pain et Copains
• Allow TEN MINUTES from the apartment to the bakery: leave rue Sainte-Claire by about 07:10
• Ticket office is 10 m from the station exit; or buy on the bus (CASH, exact change), or online at Altibus

blocks.title: Bus Y62 · Annecy → Le Grand-Bornand village
blocks.detail:
• ARVI Mobilité lines Y62/Y63, about 1h10 via Thônes and Saint-Jean-de-Sixt
• School-holiday weekday departures cluster at 08:00, 08:25, 08:55, 09:25 — this plan takes the 08:25; confirm it on the December sheet
• €8.60 single / €16 return per adult; children's fare not published — budget €50 for four
• Get off at Le Grand-Bornand VILLAGE (not Chinaillon): the sledging areas and the Rosay gondola are here
blocks.notes: Same bus continues to La Clusaz. The upper area has snowmaking and opened 7–16 December in each of the last three winters.
blocks.flag: Christmas Eve runs on a holiday timetable — confirm the return departures on the December sheet before you set out. Aim to be on a bus by 15:30.

blocks.title: La Grenouille — village sledging
blocks.detail:
• 'La Grenouille au Borne': a sunny, gently sloping sledging area in the heart of the village, built for the little ones. FREE, open daily in season, helmets advised
• No lift, no ticket
• Second free area, L'Abeille at Venay, if this one is busy
• Sledge hire from the village sports shops — about €5–10 for the day
blocks.notes: Three sledges for the day, about €21.

blocks.title: Snack — the bakery bag
blocks.detail: • The bakery sandwiches — lunch is not until 13:00

blocks.title: Rosay gondola → snow tubing & La Marmotte
blocks.detail:
• PEDESTRIAN return on the Rosay gondola: €7.70 per person aged 5–74. Only UNDER-5s are free, so all four of you pay — €30.80
• At the top, 1,420 m: the SNOW-TUBING TRACK (60 m, from age 3, two tube sizes split at 120 cm), open daily from 12 December
• Beside it 'La Marmotte', a 2,600 m² sledging area inside the beginners' zone, from age 2, open daily from 19 December
• Both are free once you are up; the gondola ticket is the cost
• Leave the top by 12:35 — the ride down is about ten minutes
blocks.notes: Gondola €30.80 plus tubing. Tubing price per session is NOT published — budget €30 for the kids and confirm at the ticket office.
blocks.flag: Both areas are listed as snow-and-weather dependent. Check the day before on legrandbornand.com.

blocks.title: Lunch — Pizzeria Casanova, Le Grand-Bornand
blocks.detail:
• 67 route de la vallée du Bouchet, village centre — a few minutes from the gondola base, by the shuttle stop
• Family restaurant, high chairs. Savoyard, pizzas, pasta, salads, omelettes
• MENU GOURMI, children: €10 — mini pizza, mini tartiflette, ham and fries or ham and spaghetti, plus two scoops of ice cream
• Pizzas €12.50–15.50; half pizza with green salad €11–13.50; spaghetti €12–15; tartiflette €23
• No booking needed
blocks.notes: About €50 for four on tap water: a pizza, a spaghetti bornandine and two children's menus.
blocks.flag: The tourist office has not yet published this winter's opening dates — no Grand-Bornand restaurant has, in September. Ring 04 50 02 20 88 nearer the time to confirm the 24th.

blocks.title: The village — church square, Christmas lights, a last slide
blocks.detail:
• Le Grand-Bornand is a working Savoyard village, not a purpose-built resort: the baroque church, wooden chalets, reblochon shops
• One last run at La Grenouille if there is energy
• Bus stop is in the village centre — be there ten minutes early

blocks.title: Bus Y62 · Le Grand-Bornand → Annecy
blocks.detail:
• Return leg of the same ticket
• Back at the gare routière about 16:40; the market is five minutes away, the apartment about twelve

blocks.title: Market stop — crêpes on the way home
blocks.detail:
• Five minutes from the coach station into the market; the chalets close early on the 24th (about 19:00)
• Bridges the gap to a 19:15 dinner

blocks.title: Back at the apartment — dry out, dress up
blocks.detail:
• Wet gear onto the drying rack and the radiators, everyone through the shower, then into something decent for Christmas Eve
• Presents organised for the morning
• LAST SHOP BEFORE CHRISTMAS: Monoprix shuts at 20:45 tonight and everything is closed tomorrow. Christmas breakfast, lunch bits and tomorrow night's supper all have to be in the flat before you go out

blocks.title: Christmas Eve dinner
blocks.detail:
• Annecy restaurants run FIXED festive menus on the 24th and they sell out. Book in November, when annecy-ville.fr publishes the year's list
• Confirmed to open 24 Dec in recent years, with prices: Ô Bon Bec (€110 adult, €45 child 5–11 — the one with a real children's price), Le Clocher in Annecy-le-Vieux (€68, five courses), Brasserie Bocuse Irma on the lake (€82/€86)
• Cheaper route: Le Fréti or Le Ramoneur Savoyard if either serves a normal card on the 24th — ask when you book Tuesday's table
blocks.notes: Budgeted at €215 for four — two adult festive menus at about €80 plus two children at about €25–45. Ô Bon Bec at €310 is the ceiling.
blocks.flag: A five-course menu starting at 19:30 ends after 21:30. Book the EARLIEST sitting offered, and ask whether the children's menu can be served fast.

days.title: Christmas Day — presents, the lake, a Savoyard lunch

blocks.title: Presents & a slow breakfast
blocks.detail:
• No fixed start. Presents in the living room, then breakfast in the flat from what you bought on the 24th
• Every shop and nearly every bakery is shut today — this is the day the kitchen earns its keep
• Nespresso machine, oven and microwave are all here
blocks.notes: Groceries, not a restaurant — bought the night before.

blocks.title: Christmas morning on the lake
blocks.detail:
• Pont des Amours, the Jardins de l'Europe, out along the Pâquier
• Free, ten minutes from the door

blocks.title: Christmas lunch — Le Ramoneur Savoyard
blocks.detail:
• 7 rue Grenette, old town — six minutes on foot
• The €21 formules and the €25 menu du jour are EXCLUDED on public holidays, so Christmas Day starts at L'Annecien, €31.50: starter, escalope in reblochon sauce or diots in red wine with polenta, then farm cheese or the chef's dessert
• MENU ENFANT 'P'tits Malins' €12.90
• Reserve: 04 50 51 29 03 — and ask specifically whether they open on the 25th at midday
blocks.notes: About €89 for four on tap water: two L'Annecien and two children's menus. UPGRADE OPTION: Brasserie Bocuse Irma on the lake is confirmed open for lunch on 25 December in recent years, festive menu €82/€86 per adult — about €220 for four with the children eating à la carte.
blocks.flag: FAR fewer kitchens open on the 25th than the 24th. Book this in November alongside Christmas Eve; fallback Brasserie des Européens (open every day per its site, 04 50 45 00 81).

blocks.title: Basilique de la Visitation — the view
blocks.detail:
• Twenty minutes uphill from the old town to the basilica on its terrace: the whole lake, the town, the Semnoz above
• Free
• Skip if it is raining

blocks.title: Back at the apartment — Christmas afternoon
blocks.detail:
• Nothing planned
• Goûter in the flat about 16:45 — cake and hot drinks from the Christmas Eve shop
• Dark by 16:50; the balcony looks onto the courtyard
blocks.flag: OPTIONAL SECOND SEMNOZ: if everyone wants snow on Christmas Day, a 13:00 taxi up and a 16:00 taxi down fits around lunch — swap this block and the basilica for it. About €100 in taxis; the station and the sledging run on the 25th.

blocks.title: Christmas supper — cooked in the flat
blocks.detail:
• After a €103 lunch nobody needs a second restaurant meal, and almost nothing is open anyway
• Soup, cheese, charcuterie, bread and whatever the kids will actually eat — all bought at Monoprix on the 24th
• Full kitchen: oven, hob, microwave, dishwasher
blocks.notes: Groceries for four, bought on the 24th. This is the single biggest saving from having a kitchen — the hotel-bar version of this evening was budgeted at $35 and depended on the bar actually serving.
blocks.flag: If you would rather eat out: Brasserie Saint Maurice, 9 rue du Collège Chapuisien, continuous service (04 50 51 24 49) — five minutes away, but confirm it is trading on the 25th.

days.title: Annecy — the rink, the old town, one last raclette

blocks.title: Breakfast — Pain et Copains
blocks.detail: • Open Saturday from 06:30

blocks.title: Old town — the last Christmas-market morning
blocks.detail:
• Rue Sainte-Claire, the Palais de l'Isle, the market chalets in daylight
• Free

blocks.title: Lunch — market chalets, Place Saint-Maurice
blocks.detail: • Tartiflette, sausages, crêpes from the chalets — standing tables
blocks.notes: About €30 for four on tap water.

blocks.title: Bus or taxi to Patinoire Jean Régis
blocks.detail: • 90 chemin des Fins, 2 km north — a €10 taxi, or SIBRA bus from the station (about 10 minutes)

blocks.title: Ice skating — Patinoire Jean Régis
blocks.detail:
• Olympic-size indoor rink with a 'Jardin de Glace' beginners' zone for ages 3–8
• UNDER-5s FREE; adult entry about €4.80, skate hire about €3.50; roughly €25 for four
• Regular Saturday public session 14:00–17:00; holiday hours not yet published — call 04 50 57 56 02
blocks.flag: If the holiday session is at a different time, the market rink in the Jardins de l'Europe is the walk-in fallback.

blocks.title: Back to the apartment
blocks.detail: • Taxi or bus back to the station, then about twelve minutes into the old town

blocks.title: Goûter — a café on rue Sainte-Claire
blocks.detail: • Cake and hot drinks under the arcades, on your own street

blocks.title: Pack
blocks.detail:
• Pack tonight, properly. CHECKOUT IS 11:00 tomorrow, not midday — there is no slack in the morning
• Wet gear into plastic bags; anything still damp goes on the rack overnight
• Run a last wash tonight if you want to fly home with clean clothes
• Strip nothing — Julien does not ask guests to launder linen

blocks.title: Dinner — Le Fréti, the raclette
blocks.detail:
• 12 rue Sainte-Claire — raclette this time
• Farmhouse Savoy raclette IGP €21 a head, AS MUCH AS YOU LIKE, with potatoes, gherkins and onions
• House rule: when an all-you-can-eat raclette is ordered, everyone else at the table takes a main course rather than a starter — the children's Brisgotte at €12.50 counts
• Reserve 04 50 51 29 52 on the same call as Tuesday
blocks.notes: About €67 for four on tap water: two raclettes and two Brisgottes.

days.title: Annecy → Paris CDG — one train, no changes

blocks.title: Breakfast — Pain et Copains
blocks.detail:
• 42 rue Vaugelas, about ten minutes from rue Sainte-Claire — worth the walk because it is OPEN SUNDAY 07:00–13:00 when most bakeries are not
• Eat there, and buy the travelling lunch at the same time: sandwiches and wraps about €6–7, pastries, water — enough for lunch on the train
blocks.notes: About €38 for breakfast and the train lunch together, water only.

blocks.title: Finish packing
blocks.detail:
• CHECKOUT IS 11:00 — an hour earlier than a hotel would be, so this is the one morning with no slack
• Everything out of the drying rack and the bathroom; check the sofa bed for stray toys
• No passports needed today — this routing never leaves France

blocks.title: Last look at the lake
blocks.detail:
• Bags packed and left in the flat. Down the Thiou, over the Pont des Amours and back — forty minutes
• Back at the door by 10:50

blocks.title: Lock up and go
blocks.detail:
• Last sweep, keys back in the box, message Julien that you are out
• Nothing to settle at a desk — the taxe de séjour was inside the $1,273.81

blocks.title: Walk to the station with the bags
blocks.detail:
• About seven minutes unencumbered, allow fifteen to twenty with four people and winter luggage
• Mostly flat, through the old town and along rue Vaugelas

blocks.title: Annecy station — board
blocks.detail:
• A long buffer by design — an 11:00 checkout leaves nowhere to wait indoors otherwise
• Platform posts about 20 minutes ahead
• Reserved seats — book four together, luggage-rack end if the seat map allows

blocks.title: TGV INOUI 6972 · Annecy → Paris Gare de Lyon
blocks.detail:
• 3h46, DIRECT — zero changes, one seat the whole way
• Runs on Sunday 27 December: confirmed on the published timetable. Fallbacks the same day: 15:29→19:14 and 17:29→21:16
• Domestic TGV, so the Carte Avantage PRICE CAP applies — an adult never pays more than €89, children −60%
blocks.notes: Budgeted at $215 for four. Floor about $150 at advance fares; ceiling about $270 at the cap. Book the moment sales open on 30 September — on an EXCHANGEABLE fare, so a better option appearing in November costs nothing to switch to.
blocks.flag: Sales open 30 September — book that morning, on an exchangeable fare.

blocks.title: Lunch on board — the bakery bag
blocks.detail:
• The bakery sandwiches at your seats
• Le Bistro bar car is in coach 4 or 14

blocks.title: Bar-car break
blocks.detail: • Croissants €2.70 each

blocks.title: Gare de Lyon — out to the car
blocks.detail:
• PRE-BOOKED car meets you on the concourse with your name on a sign (G7 app, or any Paris transfer firm) — a Sunday TGV full of returning skiers can mean a 20–30 minute rank queue
• If you queue instead: the official rank is outside the Hall 1 / Grandes Lignes exit, signposted TAXIS — marked rank only

blocks.title: Taxi · Gare de Lyon → Hyatt House
blocks.detail:
• One car, station door to hotel door
• Ask for a van (monospace) so four people and the winter bags fit in one car
• Say the hotel by name: Hyatt House Paris Charles de Gaulle, rue de la Belle Étoile, Roissy-en-France
• 25.5 km via the A3. Google, set to Sunday 27 December, gives typically 30–55 minutes — this block allows the worst case
• Roughly €60–75 on the meter; €10–15 more pre-booked
blocks.notes: The regulated €56 flat fare covers Paris ⇄ the AIRPORT only; the hotel sits five minutes past it, so this runs on the meter. Budgeted at €75 pre-booked.
blocks.flag: Cheaper: RER D → Gare du Nord, RER B → CDG, then the hotel shuttle — €42 in fares plus €8 in Navigo Easy cards, about 60 minutes. Worth €16 only if everyone is fresh.

blocks.title: Check in — Hyatt House Paris Charles de Gaulle
blocks.detail:
• Kitchenette-equipped suites, free airport shuttle, about fifteen minutes from the terminals
• CONFIRM the first shuttle departure tomorrow — you need to be at CDG by about 06:40

ideas.name: 🗺️ WHY ANNECY — what this version changes, and what it costs you

items.name: This is the same trip with the six mountain nights moved from Chamonix to Annecy. Paris (17–21), the CDG night (27) and every flight are unchanged.
WHAT YOU GAIN

ONE DIRECT TRAIN each way. Paris → Annecy 09:46→13:29 on the 21st; Annecy → Paris 12:29→16:15 on the 27th. No Geneva, no border, no coach, no Le Fayet branch line. Both are domestic TGV INOUI, so the Carte Avantage €89 cap applies both ways.
The 27th ends at the airport hotel at 17:30 instead of 19:30 — dinner at six, kids down by eight, before a 05:30 wake-up.
Christmas in a proper town: the Noël des Alpes market, an outdoor rink in the gardens, a château, the lake — all on foot from the door.
Lodging: one apartment in the old town for all four of you, $1,273.81 all in — about $100 under Cham sud in cash, with no Marriott points spent.
The snow is cheaper: Semnoz is a €2 city bus away and the sledging is free.
WHAT YOU GIVE UP
Waking up in the mountains. Annecy sits at 450 m; snow in town at Christmas is rare. The snow is a bus ride away — about an hour each time.

Planpraz, Argentière, the Mont-Blanc Express, lunch in Italy through the tunnel — and, in this version, the Mer de Glace. The Chamonix day trip was removed because it was 90 minutes each way on a coach.
Mont Blanc. You do not see it this week.

THE TRANSPORT HONESTY: by bus, every snow outing from Annecy is an hour or more — Semnoz 60, Le Grand-Bornand 70. So this version has exactly ONE bus day (Le Grand-Bornand, Thursday) and does Semnoz by TAXI — 25 minutes, about €100 for the day. Christmas Day and the 26th are on foot. That is one long ride in six days, not four.

BOOKED — 'Lovely apartment in the heart of the old town', 18 Rue Sainte-Claire, 74000 Annecy. Airbnb confirmation HM9BBY93ET. Six nights, 21–27 December, entire apartment, 4 guests maximum. $1,273.81 all in, charged to Visa 6730 on 13 November 2026.

HOST: Julien, Superhost, three years hosting, +41 79 960 38 00. Co-hosts Piccolo and Marina. Rated 4.97 across 143 reviews, in Airbnb's top 10% of homes, and carrying the 'perfect ratings from families' badge — 100% of families who stayed in the past year rated it five stars.

THE FLAT: one bedroom with a queen, living room with a 160 cm sofa bed for the children, bathroom with a SEPARATE WC, balcony onto a quiet interior courtyard. Full kitchen — oven, microwave, dishwasher, Nespresso. Washing machine, drying rack, central heating and a portable heater. Linen and towels provided. Crib available. First floor up an outside staircase, which may be icy in late December.

CHECK-IN: posted as 'after 16:00', by KEYPAD — no host to meet and no closing time. EARLY ENTRY AGREED at 14:00: Julien confirmed by message on 16 September that his cleaner normally finishes by 13:00, has the date in her calendar and has said yes; he calls it guaranteed with very low risk of change, worst case being that you leave the bags while she finishes. That is what lets the plan keep the 09:46 train. CHECKOUT 11:00, an hour earlier than the hotel would have been; Day 12 is built around that.

WALKING, from the host's own published list: old town 0 minutes (you are on it), castle 3, lake 4, train station 7. Le Fréti is six doors down at number 12. Markets on the street Sunday, Tuesday and Friday.
CANCELLATION: free until 16:00 on 21 November; partial refund until 16:00 on 14 December.

TWO THINGS TO HANDLE: there is NO CARBON MONOXIDE ALARM — Airbnb flags it and suggests a portable detector, worth €20 for six nights with two children. And rue Sainte-Claire is PEDESTRIAN, so the Semnoz taxi on the 22nd cannot reach the door; agree a pickup point at Pont Perrière when you book it.

WHAT THIS REPLACED: two Moxy rooms, one on 175,000 Marriott points plus a Free Night Award and one on cash at about $900. Both Marriott reservations, 71595872 and 71612016, were CANCELLED on 16 September.

PACK FOR THIRTEEN DAYS, NO LAUNDRY. That is the call, and it is worth knowing what it costs: roughly a checked bag. Underwear and socks alone go from 12 pieces to 24. The apartment does have a washing machine if you change your mind — the two natural windows are the 22nd at 15:30 and Christmas afternoon from 16:05 — but nothing below assumes you will touch it.

MERINO IS WHAT MAKES THIRTEEN DAYS WORK. With no wash, base layers are the only things you rewear, and merino goes three or four days without holding smell where cotton goes one. Three merino base tops cover the trip; three cotton ones would not cover five days.

DRYING IS NOT WASHING. The snow gear comes back soaked on the 22nd and again on the 24th whatever you decide about laundry. The rack and the portable heater are what dry it overnight, and both are already in the plan — 15:30 on the 22nd, 17:10 on the 24th.

TWO CLIMATES, NOT ONE. Paris is 8°C / 2°C and wet — eleven rainy days in an average December — so that leg is about staying dry, not warm. Annecy town is 5°C / −1°C, colder and clearer. Only two days are genuinely cold: Semnoz on the 22nd at 1,699 m, roughly 8°C below the town and so about −3°C with wind and sun off the snow, and Le Grand-Bornand on the 24th in between. Eleven days of rain shell, two days of real gear.

THREE LAYERS DO EVERY DAY OF THE TRIP. BASE — merino or synthetic, never cotton, two sets. MID — one fleece or light down. SHELL — one waterproof hooded jacket, and this is the piece that earns its place twice: it is the Paris rain coat AND the sledging jacket. One jacket doing both jobs is the single biggest saving in the bag.

ONLY FIVE THINGS ARE SNOW-SPECIFIC: waterproof over-trousers, waterproof gloves, thick socks, a warm hat, and sunglasses or goggles. Sledging is wetter than skiing because you sit in it, so waterproof matters more than warm — and knit gloves are useless the moment they are wet.
ONE PAIR OF BOOTS does Paris rain, Annecy cobbles and both sledging days: waterproof, warm, real grip. Wear them on the plane on the 16th, since they are the heaviest thing you own.

SMART CASUAL, WORN THREE TIMES. Dinner at Francette on the 18th, Christmas Eve dinner and Christmas lunch are the three evenings worth dressing for. One dress shirt, dark jeans and the boots covers all three — no jacket or tie required.

BAGS: one checked bag and one backpack, with the shell and the boots worn. Cabin-only does not survive the no-laundry decision — thirteen days of underwear and socks fills a carry-on by itself. The TGV is not the constraint — it allows two bags up to 70 × 90 × 50 cm plus a hand item. THE 27TH IS THE CONSTRAINT: you carry everything down an outside staircase that may be iced, then 700 m along a pedestrian street to Annecy station, with no taxi access. Keep a full change and the base layer set in the backpack — a delayed bag on the 17th means a December in Paris with what you are standing in.

TWO THINGS TO SETTLE: Delta’s checked allowance on HZHPVG is unconfirmed — check it in My Trips alongside the seats and the children’s meals. And Christmas presents either travel or get bought; the market chalets and Monoprix are both on the walk home, and buying there costs no luggage.

ideas.name: 🛷 THE SNOW — where, how much, and the one risk

items.name: LE SEMNOZ (22nd; optional 25th) — 1,450–1,700 m, directly above the lake. FREE toboggan piste, 09:00–17:00 daily; NO LIFT — you walk back up the left-hand side. Sledge hire €5 half-day / €8 day at the chalet nordique de la Forêt; no advance booking is possible. Also free at the summit: marked zones for parets and yooners. NOTE: the Semnoz's snow-tubing track is a SUMMER attraction beside the summer toboggan run — there is no winter tubing here. Restaurants: Le Châtillon at the foot of the pistes on the Annecy side (open every midday Dec–Mar, menu enfant €12, 04 50 05 45 83); Le 1407 is a winter-only snack bar on the Bauges-side car park, over the ridge, and publishes no menu. Bus S1/S2 from Annecy Gare, about 60 minutes, standard €2 SIBRA fare, DAILY 20 Dec–4 Jan; departures 07:30, 08:30, 09:30, 10:30, 12:00, 13:15; returns 10:40, 11:45, 14:25, 15:45, 16:45, 17:45, 18:15 (2025–26 sheet). REDUCED service on 24 December confirmed for 2025. The plan uses a TAXI instead (25 minutes, roughly €35–55 each way, Taxi74 06 64 12 58 66) so that Semnoz is not an hour each way.

THE SEMNOZ RECORD, since you asked: shut over Christmas in 2018 (closed from 24 Dec — too warm for the new snow cannons) and in 2022 (from 22 Dec, sledging area included, only the baby slope open); opened on time on 16 Dec 2023; opened 21 Dec 2024, partially, 'thanks to recent snowfall'. Two of the last eight winters, and one near miss. Check semnoz.fr's live status the night before; if it is shut, swap Tuesday with the Grand-Bornand day.

LE GRAND-BORNAND (24th) — 1,000 m village, 1,300 m+ at Chinaillon and the top of Rosay. Two FREE sledging areas in the village (La Grenouille at Borne, L'Abeille at Venay) — the 5-year-old needs no lift. Rosay gondola pedestrian ticket €7.70 return per person aged 5+, under-5 free; snow-tubing track at the top (from age 3, price not published); 'La Marmotte' 2,600 m² sledging area at the summit. Bus Y62/Y63 from the gare routière, 1h10, €8.60 single / €16 return adult, child fare not published. Lunch: Pizzeria Casanova, 67 route de la vallée du Bouchet, menu enfant €10 — winter opening dates not yet published, ring 04 50 02 20 88.
LA CLUSAZ (swap-in) — same bus, one hour. Three free sledging slopes; outdoor rink €6.50 adult / €5 child 5–16, skates €4–5; Pizza Minut has a children's pizza.

SNOW REALITY: at village level (Annecy 450 m, Grand-Bornand 1,000 m) Christmas snow is a coin flip. The Grand-Bornand gondola day happens at 1,300 m+ with snowmaking, where it is not; Semnoz at 1,450–1,700 m is the one with a record.

REMOVED: the Chamonix / Mer de Glace day trip — 90 minutes each way on a coach was the one ride you said you did not want. It can come back as a single long day if you change your mind: BlaBlaCar from the gare routière about 08:30, Montenvers family pass €148.30, first train 10:00.
